passage:
Subject: Sorry I did not tell you

Dear Hansa,

You asked why I stopped picking up your calls. I failed one paper in November. I was so scared of Papa's face that I said nothing, and I told myself I would fix it quietly. The backlog form was due on 10 January, and I did not fill it. I thought, one more day. The deadline passed. Now the department says I will need to wait a whole extra term. Papa found out from the notice sent home, and he was not angry about the failure. He was hurt that I had hidden it. The silence cost more than the paper ever did. I am going to the advisor on Monday. Can you come with me?

Vasudha

qa.q: When was the backlog form due?
qa.a: The backlog form was due on 10 January.

qa.q: What was Vasudha feeling when hiding the result?
qa.a: Vasudha felt afraid of Papa's reaction and hoped the problem could be fixed quietly.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Vasudha have used in November, and why?
qa.a: Vasudha could have told Papa or a trusted adult at once and asked the advisor about the form, because the deadline was the real danger and it needed people who could help.

qa.q: How does Papa see what happened?
qa.a: Papa was not angry about the failure but hurt that it was hidden, so Papa's worry is about the silence and not only the paper.

grounding: Shows hiding a failed result out of fear, skipping the forms, and finding that missed deadlines made things worse than the failure itself.

subtype: Approach: avoidance and hiding the result [Pitfall]
passage: Hrithik, you asked why I'm repeating second year. Okay. I'll tell you the whole thing, because I don't want you to do what I did. I'm Siddharth. Last June I failed two subjects. My father had told half the relatives I'd get a distinction. I couldn't say it. So I said nothing. The backlog exam form was due on 15 July. I saw the notice. I told myself I'd fill it after I found the right moment to tell Papa. The moment never came. The deadline passed. Then the next exam cycle filled up before I'd even checked. By December the college told me I couldn't move to third year with those credits missing. Two failed papers became a lost year. And I still had to tell Papa, only now the news was much worse. If you ever fail something, fill the form first. Tell them second.

qa.q: When was the backlog exam form due?

qa.a: Siddharth was afraid of Papa's reaction, since Papa had told relatives about a distinction, and felt too ashamed to say it.

qa.q: What would you change first in how Siddharth handled it?
qa.a: Fill the backlog form before the deadline, then tell the family, perhaps with help from an advisor or a trusted relative.

qa.q: How might Papa feel hearing the news in December?
qa.a: Papa is likely more hurt and worried than he would have been in June, since hiding it turned two papers into a lost year.

grounding: Shows a student who, afraid of the family's reaction, hides the failure and skips the backlog form, so lapsed deadlines make things worse than the original failure.

passage: I'm Saurabh, and Deepak is my cousin; we share a room at his parents' house in Nashik. I noticed the change in July. Deepak stopped talking about college. When his mother asked about results, he said, "Not out yet." They had been out for two weeks. One evening I saw a notice on his screen: "Last date for backlog exam registration: 31 July." He closed the tab fast. I asked if he was okay. He said, "Just leave it." August came. He didn't register. In September a letter came from the university saying his next attempt would be the following summer, and that he couldn't carry the missing credits into final year. His mother read it at the dining table. I've never heard a room that quiet. I can't know everything he was feeling, but I saw his face. He looked less scared than exhausted.

qa.q: What was the last date for backlog registration?
Why do you think Deepak closed the tab so fast?
qa.a: Deepak was probably afraid and ashamed, wanting to avoid facing the failure and his mother's reaction.

qa.q: What else could Deepak have done in July?
qa.a: Deepak could have registered before 31 July and told his mother, maybe with Saurabh beside him for support.

qa.q: How is Deepak's mother affected by the letter?
qa.a: Deepak's mother learns the truth all at once from a letter, and the silence suggests shock and hurt at being kept in the dark.

grounding: Illustrates a student hiding a failed result from family and letting the backlog deadline lapse, which makes the situation worse than the failure itself.
